lessons.title: Hardware, software and the computer system

objectives: Define a computer and name its four basic functions
Classify software as system or application software
Name the main parts inside the system unit
reviewNotes: Classification of software (system / application / programming) follows the usual textbook split; check the exact wording used by the syllabus.

blocks.title: What a computer is
blocks.md: A **computer** is an electronic machine that accepts **input**, **processes** it following stored instructions, produces **output** and can **store** results. The cycle is often written \*Input - Process - Output - Storage\*.

blocks.title: Hardware and software
blocks.md: **Hardware** is every physical part you can touch: keyboard, monitor, CPU, memory chips, disks. **Software** is the set of programs (instructions) that tell the hardware what to do. A computer without software cannot do useful work; software without hardware cannot run.

blocks.caption: A computer takes input, processes it with the CPU, gives output and can store the result.
blocks.alt: Four boxes joined by arrows: input, processing, output and storage.

blocks.title: Types of software
blocks.md:
- **System software** manages the computer: operating system, utility programs (antivirus, disk cleaner), device drivers.
- **Application software** does tasks for the user: word processor, spreadsheet, browser, games.
- **Programming software** (compilers, interpreters) is used to create other programs.

blocks.title: Common mistakes
blocks.md:
- A file, a photo or a program is **not** hardware: it is data or software stored \*on\* hardware.
- The **CPU** is not the whole computer; the \*system unit\* (case) holds the motherboard, CPU, RAM, storage and power supply.
- Windows, Linux and Android are operating systems, **not** application programs.

blocks.title: Example 1 - Classify
blocks.statement: A school bursar in Bamenda uses a spreadsheet to total fees, an antivirus to protect the PC and a laser printer. Classify each item.
steps: Spreadsheet: it does a user task (totals) so it is application software.
Antivirus: it protects and maintains the system so it is system (utility) software.
Laser printer: a physical device so it is hardware (an output device).
blocks.answer: Spreadsheet = application software; antivirus = system software; printer = hardware.

blocks.title: Example 2 - IPO
blocks.statement: Identify the input, process and output when a student types 12 and 8 and the computer displays 20.
steps: Input: the numbers 12 and 8 typed on the keyboard.
Output: 20 displayed on the monitor; it may be saved to disk (storage).

blocks.title: Three kinds of device
blocks.md:
- **Input devices** send data in: keyboard, mouse, scanner, microphone, digital camera, touch screen, barcode reader.
- **Output devices** present results: monitor, printer, speakers, projector.
- **Storage devices** keep data: hard disk, solid-state drive, flash drive, memory card, optical disc.

blocks.title: Memory and storage
blocks.md: **RAM** (random access memory) holds programs and data in use; it is fast and **volatile** (it loses its contents when power is off). **ROM** (read-only memory) holds start-up instructions and keeps them without power. **Secondary storage** (disks, flash drives) keeps files permanently but is slower than RAM.

blocks.caption: A table with three columns listing example input, output and storage devices.
blocks.alt: Table: input devices keyboard, mouse, scanner; output devices monitor, printer, speaker; storage devices hard disk, flash drive, memory card.

blocks.title: Storage units
blocks.md: A **bit** is 0 or 1. **8 bits = 1 byte**. In school computing we use 1 KB = 1024 bytes, 1 MB = 1024 KB, 1 GB = 1024 MB, 1 TB = 1024 GB. (Some makers use 1000; this lesson uses 1024.)

blocks.title: Common mistakes
blocks.md:
- A touch screen is **both** input and output.
- RAM is not permanent storage: unsaved work is lost in a power cut (a real risk in many towns).
- Do not confuse \*memory\* (RAM) with \*storage\* (disk), even though both are measured in bytes.

blocks.title: Example 1 - Which device?
blocks.statement: A shop in Kumba wants to (a) read product codes at the till, (b) print receipts, (c) back up daily sales. Choose a device for each.
steps: (a) Reading product codes is input: a barcode reader.
(b) Printing receipts is output: a printer.
(c) Backing up needs storage: an external disk or flash drive.
blocks.answer: Barcode reader, printer, external disk or flash drive.

blocks.title: Example 2 - Units
blocks.statement: How many bytes are in 3 KB, and how many MB are in 5 GB?

exercises.source: Original exercise written for CastBridge, in the style of the curriculum
exercises.prompt: Explain why a computer needs both hardware and software. Give one example of each.
exercises.model: Hardware provides the physical parts that carry out operations (e.g. the CPU or the keyboard). Software gives the instructions that tell the hardware what to do (e.g. an operating system). Without software the hardware does nothing useful; without hardware the software has nothing to run on.
exercises.rubric: 1 mark each: role of hardware, role of software, one correct example of each (3 marks).
